title: CORRECTION to SIG-W-20261014-025: the IMO table marks Cape Dao SUNK and GFS Pride is the THIRD vessel sunk since February 28, not the second; none of the three is in FALCON's loss census
origin: IMO Middle East incidents table (as at 14 October 2026), fetched by sweep leg A
corrects_direction: FLIPS loss-ordinal leg — GFS PRIDE is the IMO's third sunk vessel, not second; Cape Dao is marked Sunk on the IMO table (was 'reportedly sinking, single source')
dispatch_note: Self-correction found by tonight's full re-verify (research/2026-10-14_iran-full-sweep/leg-A-shipping.md section 2). R1 row COR-20261014-31 in the same commit. -025's other claims (cause INDETERMINATE, mine CLAIM-ONLY, Aramco threat) stand.
body: -025 said 'the IMO counts GFS PRIDE as the SECOND vessel lost since February 28 (the first being Safeen Prestige)' and that Cape Dao was 'reportedly sinking after a failed salvage (Vanguard, single source)'. The IMO Middle East incidents table (fetched; as at 14 October 2026: 113 incidents, 24 seafarer fatalities) now marks THREE ships 'Sunk': SAFEEN PRESTIGE (4 March, 2 nm N of Oman), CAPE DAO (struck 23 September, 15 nm NE of Khasab per the IMO, one seafarer killed; sinking date not stated) and GFS PRIDE (13 October, Strait of Hormuz). Reuters (October 14), analysing IMO data, calls GFS PRIDE and Cape Dao 'the second and third vessels to have sunk'. So GFS PRIDE is the third loss on the IMO basis and Cape Dao's sinking is confirmed at the IMO, not single-source. For FALCON: none of these three is in FALCON's 3-loss census (Faize Noore Oliya, a dhow, 8/4; Kylo 9/5; Riesco 9/8), and Kylo and Riesco do not appear on the IMO table, so the two counts measure different sets; UKMTO separately cites '5 confirmed total losses YTD' and CENTCOM '10 tankers destroyed' since 7/14. Never add these. FALCON's ledger places Cape Dao about 2.5 nm off Musandam vs the IMO's 15 nm NE of Khasab. What stands from -025: GFS PRIDE's cause is INDETERMINATE (MPA 'unknown projectiles'; the IRGC Navy mine claim names no ship and is CLAIM-ONLY); no confirmed mine detonation; the Aramco-shareholder line is a threat statement.
sources: IMO Middle East incidents table, as at 14 October 2026 (fetched by sweep leg A)
Reuters, October 14 2026 (IMO-data analysis), as read by sweep leg A
ask: FALCON: reconcile your 3-loss census against the IMO's three 'Sunk' rows (different sets) and record Cape Dao's sinking; the count, its basis and any ladder #2 consequence are yours.

title: Iran full re-verify, week to October 15: FAL-01 stays firm-negative; IMO lists three ships sunk, none in FALCON's census; Riyadh-airport deaths appear to cross FALCON's casualty bar; no ladder item fired
origin: WALTER full re-verify, three read-only verify legs, 2026-10-15 ~01:15Z
Saudi Energy Ministry / GACA via SPA relays
IEA OMR and OPEC MOMR October
confidence_language: multi-source; several primaries unread at source
dispatch_note: Will-directed full weekly Iran re-verify (calendar due 10/15; the MPA-confirmed GFS Pride sinking was also a ladder trigger). Anchor IRAN_WAR.md re-stamped: last full sweep 2026-10-15, next ~10-22; superseded lines rotated verbatim to HISTORY. Guard corpus read whole by each leg. FALCON dark since 10/10 with its 7-day mark review due 10/14: doorbell pointer to PROME in this commit. WALTER does not grade; every 'for FALCON' item is an owner call.
body: Production: GATE 1 / FAL-01 stays FIRM-NEGATIVE. Every confirmed hit 10/08-10/15 is out of class: the Aramco Dhahran HQ office tower on 10/13 (Energy Ministry: 'limited fire', no casualties; Reuters sources: extensive damage to the top floors; production unaffected) and the Riyadh and Dammam airports. The only in-class candidate is Abqaiq smoke on 10/08 (Soar Atlas imagery, Tasnim; no Saudi, Aramco or wire confirmation). A ballistic missile aimed at Haradh (southern Ghawar) on 10/13 was intercepted (coalition). FALCON's production rung D 85->92 stays armed, not fired. No force majeure anywhere (Aramco, ADNOC, KPC, SOMO; QatarEnergy's March LNG declaration is pre-existing). Losses: GFS PRIDE sank (MPA and IMO); cause INDETERMINATE (projectile per MPA/Reuters security sources; the IRGC mine claim names no ship). The IMO table marks three ships Sunk (Safeen Prestige 3/4, Cape Dao, GFS PRIDE), none in FALCON's 3-loss census (correction SIG-W-20261014-031). No confirmed mine detonation; CENTCOM says it cleared mines from the main lanes on 10/8. Hull war (UKMTO's own products, read from its posted images): 159-26 to 173-26 = 12 attack warnings 10/09-10/13 (six on 10/11, four on 10/13) plus 2 advisories; 10 in Hormuz, 1 in the Gulf off the UAE (GEM NO.2), 1 in the Gulf of Oman (PETRO DOLPHIN at Sohar, drone, 2 missing), none in the Red Sea; container ships are now being hit; none dated 10/12 or 10/14. IMO incidents 113, 24 seafarer deaths (as at 10/14). Ship names are inferred, none UKMTO-named. Transits stay at floors: PortWatch 29 in the 7 days to 10/11 (4.1/day, about 4.7% of the 88/day baseline); Anadolu's count fell 32 to 6 (10/8-10/12); Kpler barrels 20.8 to 10.4 to 8.3 mb (10/8, 10/12, 10/13); CENTCOM's '>19 mb' on 10/12 is about twice Kpler's figure; never blend vendors. Red Sea quiet. Saudi-Houthi: GACA confirms 12 killed and 309 injured at Riyadh airport on 10/10 (13 after a later death), 1 killed on 10/11 and 3 on 10/08; FALCON's casualty-ratchet lighting bar was 12 confirmed killed, so it appears crossed (FALCON grades). Houthi claims widened (Shedgum, Tanajib, the Riyadh refinery: unconfirmed). US and diplomacy: no US or Israeli strike on Iranian territory found 10/08-10/14 (search and tracker based; CENTCOM unread at source). Trump 10/08: no attack before the 11/3 midterms; 10/13: 'decision on Iran very soon' (statements, not decisions). The blockade is CENTCOM-dated from 7/14; Ocean Molica disabled 10/10. A 30-government statement (10/12) recognizes the UK's attribution of the 9/27 RAF Fairford plot to Iran. Rezaei (10/11): the US reply is 'inadequate', some of Iran's seven conditions accepted and Iran-Oman joint management rejected, both per Iran; Baghaei (10/12): still reviewing, via Pakistan and Qatar; Oman-Pakistan met 10/14 with no date. No dated framework; the Iran-Oman corridor coordinates are undated, unpublished and unconfirmed by Oman. Ladder: #1, #3, #3b, #4, #5, #6, #7 NOT FIRED; #2's sinking facts are on record for FALCON, its mine limb NOT FIRED; FALCON's C->B and D->C conditions both unmet. Supply: IEA (10/14) September Gulf crude exports +4.4 to 13.9 mb/d; OPEC MOMR Saudi ~8.0 mb/d on secondary sources vs 8.372 self-reported (two bases).
ask: FALCON: your 7-day mark review (due 10/14) can run on this sweep. Items for you: the IMO-vs-census loss sets and Cape Dao (-031), the casualty-ratchet bar vs GACA counts, Abqaiq 10/08 and Haradh 10/13, and the inferred hull identities in leg A. BRENT: reconcile the Baltic TD3C basis (10/9 WS1,318.75 implies a prior WS1,203.75 vs the board's 1,145 for 10/2) and carry the IEA/OPEC supply prints on their own bases.
